beats.say: A test is ninety-nine percent accurate, and you test positive. How worried should you be?
Imagine a thousand people, and a condition only one of them has.
The test catches the one real case. But it also wrongly flags one percent of the healthy people. That's about ten false alarms.
So of about eleven positive results, only one is real. A positive means roughly a nine percent chance you're sick. That's why positive screens get a second test.
Rare condition, 99%-accurate test, you test positive. Roughly what are your odds of being sick here?

data.question: Rare condition, 99%-accurate test, you test positive. Roughly what are your odds of being sick here?
data.answer: About 9 percent, because false positives outnumber true ones.
